status: CONTRACT FROZEN. Not implemented in this amendment.

whyThisExists.correction: The Stage 1 isolation tests are STATIC manifest, path and import validation. They read committed planning artifacts and assert their shape. They are NOT runtime proof, and this contract stops them being described as such.
whyThisExists.actualIsolationIs: a mandatory discover-mode gate that must run inside the same runtime boundary intended for execute mode, before execute is authorized

theAcquisitionProcessReceivesNo.note: Every entry is false: none of these is present inside the acquisition runtime boundary.

runtimeHardening.writableSpace: exactly two classes: the experiment output mount (read-write), and explicitly named tmpfs paths for process and runtime temporary files. No other experiment-controlled path is writable.

mayContainOnly: package and runtime files required to execute
runtimeBundle.builtWithUnrestrictedRepositoryCopyNote: A blanket COPY of the repository is prohibited: it would place .git, artifacts/, fixtures and the eval manifest inside the boundary and silently defeat every isolation claim above.

bundleManifest.contents: every SOURCE input path and every EMITTED path, each with its SHA-256, plus the build command, tool version and metafile digest
bundleManifest.verifiedIn: generated and verified in phase 1 trusted host preparation; re-verified against the mounted bundle in isolated discover

dependencyClosureGate.why: The Stage 1 source guard inspects only the two runner files. A runner could import an apparently innocuous helper that itself imports fixtures or a truth-bearing module. First-order source inspection cannot see that; a dependency closure can.
dependencyClosureGate.ownedBy: phase 1 trusted host preparation. Isolated discover verifies the resulting bundle and manifest, but does not and cannot own the transitive proof.
dependencyClosureGate.mustGenerate: a complete dependency closure — a bundler metafile or an equivalent full module graph — enumerating EVERY source module that contributed to the built runtime, transitively, not only the runner's first-order imports

sourceMapsAndEmbeddedSources.why: A source map with inlined sourcesContent would carry prohibited file contents into the bundle even though no prohibited path appears in the emitted graph.
sourceMapsAndEmbeddedSources.rule: either emit no source maps, or emit them with sourcesContent stripped and prove no prohibited path appears in the sources array

bundleManifestMustRecord: every SOURCE input path with its SHA-256
for each production source input, the SHA-256 it has at the frozen base commit
every EMITTED runtime path with its SHA-256
the exact build tool name and version
the SHA-256 of the dependency graph / metafile itself
the designated truth-key inventory asset path and its SHA-256
the separately reviewed Stage 2 evaluation-script paths and their SHA-256 values

preIsolationBundleScan.runsIn: phase 1, on the BUILT bundle, before anything is mounted
preIsolationBundleScan.selfTriggeringDefect: A blanket executable scan for the forbidden keys would have rejected the truth-isolation scanner, which must know those keys to scan emitted evidence.
preIsolationBundleScan.sourceTextInferenceDefect: Amendment 5 solved that by inspecting the scanner's SOURCE TEXT: every frozen token had to appear somewhere, and a regex looked for some additions. That proves neither direction. A key left only in a COMMENT satisfied the presence test, and an addition outside the regex's recognized prefixes — matchesExpectedResult, for instance — widened the scanner undetected.
preIsolationBundleScan.strategy: dedicated canonical inventory ASSET; array equality is decidable, source-text presence is not

inventoryAsset.content: a bare canonical JSON array of the authoritative key names, in authoritative order, and nothing else

frozenScope: scan the RAW BYTES of every bundle file, including binary assets, for historical case IDs and historical fixture paths
require exact array equality with the authoritative inventory, order included
require the asset's exact byte digest to match the bundle manifest
permit forbidden-key strings only in that one asset
reject them in every other executable, data or configuration file
never receive or scan a Brand-value inventory
preIsolationBundleScan.brandStringsNeverScannedWhy: A legitimate transcript may naturally contain the Brand text. That is evidence, not leakage. The scan takes no Brand inventory as a parameter, so it cannot be reconfigured into comparing evidence against Brand truth.

haltCodes.BUNDLE_PROHIBITED_DEPENDENCY: a transitive source input resolves under a prohibited path
haltCodes.BUNDLE_MANIFEST_INCOMPLETE: a source or emitted path is missing from the manifest, or the metafile digest does not match
haltCodes.BUNDLE_PROHIBITED_CONTENT: the pre-isolation scan found a historical identifier, fixture path or truth-bearing key
haltCodes.PRODUCTION_SOURCE_DRIFTED_FROM_BASE: a production runtime source input does not match its bytes at the frozen base commit

dependencyClosureGate.directRunnerGuardIsNotTransitive: src/fixtures/eval/issue-149-acquisition-isolation.test.ts inspects the runner sources only. It is a useful first-order gate and is explicitly not a transitive proof.

frozenExceptions.reason: Mandatory deterministic incumbent Alcohol parser, reached by the UNCHANGED extractor path: field-selection.ts line 1 imports @/domain/rules/wine-alcohol-parse. Without it the direct extractLabelEvidenceDetailed route cannot run at all.
frozenExceptions.whyNotTruth: It is a bounded deterministic parser over label text. It reads no governed truth, no acceptable values and no per-case record.
frozenExceptions.priorDefect: Amendment 5 prohibited every transitive dependency under src/domain/rules/**, so host preparation would have halted with BUNDLE_PROHIBITED_DEPENDENCY while bundling the exact incumbent extractor it is required to run.

dependencyClosureGate.frozenExceptionsRule: An exception is a PATH AND CONTENT HASH pair. A different path under the same directory is not covered, and the same path with different bytes is not covered.

productionSourceBaseDriftGate.why: A bundle manifest that merely records whatever production source happened to be present proves the bundle is internally consistent, not that it is the INCUMBENT. The acquisition claims to observe the incumbent path at a named commit; that claim needs the bytes pinned to that commit.
productionSourceBaseDriftGate.appliesTo: every production source file in the dependency closure, not only the named exception
productionSourceBaseDriftGate.stage2ScriptsAreSeparate: Stage 2 acquisition scripts under the explicitly approved evaluation paths are not production sources. They are hashed and reviewed separately, and are listed distinctly in the bundle manifest.

forbiddenEvidenceKeyInventory.canonicalFormatting: a bare JSON array of the key names in authoritative order, no whitespace, one terminal newline
forbiddenEvidenceKeyInventory.keysNotRestatedHereWhy: Amendment 6 declared the asset authoritative and then copied the array into four contracts and a test, which is four more places to drift. Operative contracts reference the path and hash; the runtime, the freeze script, the bundle scanner and the consistency test all READ the asset.
forbiddenEvidenceKeyInventory.fieldNamesVersusValues: These are FIELD NAMES, prohibited inside acquisition output. The historical identifier and fixture-path VALUES are checked after sealing by the read-only identity-leak verifier, which holds an inventory the isolated runtime never receives.
forbiddenEvidenceKeyInventory.governsEveryEmittedFile: pass records, candidate records, selection records, item-level failure records, count records, manifests and provenance records alike

candidateEmissionClosureGate.theDirectRunnerRegexIsNotTransitiveNote: src/fixtures/eval/issue-149-acquisition-isolation.test.ts inspects the runner sources only. A helper the runner imports could reach a lower-level candidate function without the runner source containing a prohibited symbol. The Stage 2 source-closure gate owns the transitive property; the first-order regex does not and does not claim to.
candidateEmissionClosureGate.requiredSoleEmissionCallNote: It must be the only candidate-emission call reachable from the runner's transitive Stage 2 source closure, and it takes the complete diagnostic FieldSelection — never a caller-supplied candidate array.
candidateEmissionClosureGate.theAdapterModuleItself: scripts/eval/lib/issue-149-candidate-adapter.ts — it defines the private functions and is the one file exempt from the reference prohibition
candidateEmissionClosureGate.noRuntimeTestBackdoorNote: TEST_ONLY_candidateAdapterInternals was a real exported object holding both lower-level functions, so the private functions were reachable at runtime. It is removed; the adapter exports exactly one candidate-emission function.

mustDo: recursively list every accessible mounted file
assert known forbidden paths cannot be opened
assert the repository root is unavailable
assert the post-freeze ID map is unavailable
assert the eval manifest and fixture paths are unavailable
verify that only the four authorized experiment data mounts exist, plus the allowlisted pseudo-filesystem classes
discoverModeGate.executeAuthorizedOnlyAfter: the discover-mode evidence is reviewed and execute is explicitly authorized

writableSpaceCorrection.priorContradiction: Amendment 2 said writable space was tmpfs-only AND authorized a read-write output mount. Both could not be true.
writableSpaceCorrection.resolution: The output mount is a real read-write bind mount, not a tmpfs, so evidence survives the container. tmpfs covers only process/runtime scratch. The two are named separately.

authorizedWritablePaths.purpose: process and runtime temporary files only

mountInvariant.correction: Amendment 2 said 'exactly four mounts'. That is not implementable: every container carries required runtime mounts. The invariant is four EXPERIMENT-CONTROLLED data mounts plus an explicit allowlist of unavoidable pseudo-filesystems.
allowedPseudoFilesystemClasses: tmpfs for the explicitly named scratch paths

twoPhaseDesign.correction: Amendment 2's discover steps required the checkout, the freeze script, artifacts and the ID map — none of which exists inside the isolated boundary. The plan is split so each check runs where it can actually run.

steps: checkout and verify the Stage 1 contract package against stage-1-contract-manifest.sha256
verify the source images and the post-freeze id map
build the allowlisted runtime bundle WITHOUT an unrestricted repository COPY
generate the complete dependency closure / metafile for every runtime input module
fail closed on any transitive source input under a prohibited path
write the runtime bundle manifest: source paths, emitted paths, per-path SHA-256, build command, tool version, metafile digest
scan the BUILT bundle for historical case IDs, historical fixture paths and prohibited truth-bearing keys
prepare an initially empty output directory
phase1TrustedHostPreparation.hasAccessTo: the repository checkout, artifacts, fixtures and the post-freeze id map, because preparation legitimately needs them

mustVerify: the runtime bundle manifest, including that every mounted emitted path matches its recorded SHA-256
staged opaque image hashes and byte sizes
that only the output mount and the named tmpfs paths are writable
that forbidden paths cannot be opened
phase2IsolatedDiscover.checksMovedToPhase1Note: These require files that do not exist inside the boundary. Claiming they run inside the container would be false.
phase2IsolatedDiscover.doesNotOwn: the transitive dependency proof. It can confirm the bundle it was given matches the manifest; it cannot reconstruct how that bundle was built.

stage1ExecutionStatus: The Stage 1 trusted freeze/staging generator and its temporary reproducibility mode have run. No Stage 2 Job A workflow, truth-free preparation artifact, runtime-bundle build, discovery, execute mode or governed 115-case acquisition OCR has run.
